name: ghz
what_it_is: ghz is a command-line gRPC benchmarking and load testing tool written in Go. It sends configurable volumes of gRPC requests to a target server and reports latency distributions, error rates, and throughput metrics.
components: ghz CLI binary (cmd/ghz) — primary load generator
runner package — programmatic Go API for driving load tests
printer package — formats reports as summary, CSV, JSON, pretty, HTML, or InfluxDB line protocol
load package — pacer and worker-ticker implementations for const/step/line schedules
web sub-application — optional HTTP UI for storing and browsing historical test reports (backed by a database)
protocols: gRPC (HTTP/2) — the only supported transport protocol
gRPC with server reflection (automatic service discovery without a .proto file)
gRPC streaming: unary, client-streaming, server-streaming, and bidirectional streaming
measurement: Total request count and total wall-clock duration
Latency percentile distribution (p10, p25, p50, p75, p90, p95, p99)
Error distribution (count per error message string)
gRPC status code distribution (count per status code)
Per-request detail records (timestamp + latency + status) included in JSON/CSV output
InfluxDB line-protocol output (influx-summary and influx-details formats) for time-series ingestion
configuration: --proto / --protoset — service definition source (mutually exclusive; --proto takes precedence)
--call — fully-qualified gRPC method (package.Service/Method)
-n / --total — number of requests (default 200); ignored when -z duration is set
-c / --concurrency — concurrent worker goroutines (default 50)
--connections — number of underlying gRPC connections (default 1; concurrency spread evenly across them)
-r / --rps — rate-limit in requests per second (0 = unlimited)
--load-schedule — const | step | line load ramp profiles
--concurrency-schedule — const | step | line concurrency ramp profiles
-z / --duration — time-boxed run; overrides -n
-x / --max-duration — upper bound on wall time even when -n is set
-t / --timeout — per-request timeout (default 20s)
--connect-timeout — dial timeout (default 10s)
-d / --data or -D / --data-file — request payload as JSON or file path
-b / --binary or -B / --binary-file — pre-serialised binary protobuf payload
-m / --metadata or -M / --metadata-file — gRPC request metadata as JSON
--stream-interval / --stream-call-count / --stream-call-duration — streaming call control
--skipTLS / --insecure — disable TLS verification or use plaintext
--async — fire-and-forget mode (do not wait for response before sending next request)
-O / --format — output format: summary | csv | json | pretty | html | influx-summary | influx-details
--config — path to JSON or TOML config file containing all settings
--skipFirst — exclude the first N requests from statistics
--count-errors — include error responses in latency statistics
--cpus — pin to N OS threads (default: all available cores)
-e / --enable-compression — Gzip-compress request bodies
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection; ghz is a client-side load generator only — it cannot inject errors or delays into the server under test
Error responses from the server are captured and tallied in errorDistribution and statusCodeDistribution fields of the report
modes: Constant load: fixed RPS or fixed concurrency for a set request count or duration (default)
Step load: RPS or concurrency increases/decreases by a fixed step every step-duration
Line (linear ramp) load: RPS or concurrency changes linearly from start to end over max-duration
Async mode: requests are dispatched without waiting for previous responses, maximising in-flight count
Streaming mode: client-streaming, server-streaming, or bidirectional streaming with per-message interval and count controls
Reflection mode: service schema discovered at runtime via gRPC server reflection (no .proto file required)
Web UI mode: ghz-web HTTP server stores runs in a database and serves a browsable report dashboard
constraints: Only gRPC (HTTP/2) is supported — no HTTP/1.1, REST, or other protocols
Number of connections cannot exceed concurrency (-connections <= -concurrency); violation is a fatal config error
Binary data and --stream-dynamic-messages are mutually exclusive
When -z duration is set, -n (total requests) is ignored (overridden to MaxInt32)
Step and line load schedules require load-start, load-end, and load-step / load-step-duration to be specified
No native support for generating varied/randomised payloads beyond Go template functions in data JSON
No server-side component — ghz only generates load; the target gRPC server must be provided separately
Docker image targets a single static binary; no docker-compose file is provided in the repository
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — the repository ships only a multi-stage Dockerfile producing a static binary image
No HTTP/REST or WebSocket load testing capability
No built-in server-side fault injection or chaos tooling
No distributed/multi-node load generation (all load originates from a single process)
No authentication helpers beyond mTLS (e.g., no OAuth2 token refresh built in)
No real-time streaming dashboard — the ghz-web UI shows historical reports, not live metrics
